blocks.title: Why Structured Outputs with JSON Schema matters in a real product

spans.text: Problem statement:

A team is dealing with an invoice assistant must return machine-readable JSON that downstream code can trust. They do not need trivia about Structured Outputs with JSON Schema; they need a decision they can make, a concrete artifact they can inspect, and a way to know whether valid structured outputs on messy inputs is improving.

This lesson keeps one running case in view: JSON Schema output contract plus validation and repair loop. Every module asks what the system sees, what it changes, what can go wrong, and how a reviewer would prove the behavior before trusting it.

Before reading on, predict: if the model returns plausible JSON that violates required enum or type constraints, which part of the design would you inspect first - input, mechanism, decision rule, implementation, or monitoring?
Because this is an intermediate lesson, assume the vocabulary is learnable and spend your effort on tradeoffs, integration points, and the tests that prove the design works.

blocks.title: Runnable check: validate a structured LLM output
blocks.code:
# Structured Outputs with JSON Schema: tiny structured-output validator.
import json
raw = '{"decision": "escalate", "confidence": 0.82, "reason": "missing invoice id"}'
required = {"decision", "confidence", "reason"}
allowed_decisions = {"answer", "escalate", "refuse"}

obj = json.loads(raw)
valid = required.issubset(obj) and obj["decision"] in allowed_decisions and 0 <= obj["confidence"] <= 1
print(obj["decision"])
print("valid" if valid else "invalid")

spans.text: This is not the full production implementation of Structured Outputs with JSON Schema. It is a runnable miniature that makes the lesson's contract visible: input, decision, output, and a check tied to the running failure mode.

It prints:
escalate
valid

The output is not trusted merely because it looks like JSON. The validator checks required fields, allowed decisions, and confidence range before downstream code uses it.
